note: Adverse known answers. Tiny and Lantern steps use the cases.json/lantern-traces.json shapes; see conformance/README.md.

tiny.description: Failed roll is an accepted outcome: RNG advances, lantern stays, replay is byte-stable, the next attempt draws from the advanced state.
A rejection advances nothing; after the world changes, the same id replays the original rejection.
Harness-denied authorization and a different actor both get unauthorized, not the stored receipt.
Changing semantic input, target order or action under a used id is an integrity conflict; transport metadata alone replays.
A consumed choice replays its receipt without restoring the old view; an altered choice conflicts; a new id on the consumed offer is invalid.
A new invocation against an old view is rejected without game change.
A fault before COMMIT publishes nothing, stores no receipt and lets the same id run fresh.
Unknown COMMIT fences all work until settled; once known committed, the retry replays and nothing reruns.
Unknown COMMIT fences all work until settled; once known absent, the retry runs as new.
Committed durably but not applied in memory: fenced until recovery, then the retry replays from durable state.
A lost response does not duplicate published effects on retry.
Malformed envelopes are rejected with no state or receipt.
A non-string direction is a typed rejection.

composition.description: Shared operations cap of 2 on a self-reemitting rule: whole transaction fails, no partial state or events.
Shared events cap of 2 on a self-reemitting rule: whole transaction fails, no partial state or events.
Shared deliveries cap of 2 on a self-reemitting rule: whole transaction fails, no partial state or events.
Shared reaction_depth cap of 2 on a self-reemitting rule: whole transaction fails, no partial state or events.
Shared query_steps cap of 2 on a self-reemitting rule: whole transaction fails, no partial state or events.
Output cap is checked before publication: no partial events.
Adding past 2^31-1 is a bounds failure, never a clamp.
A follow-up due at or before the advance target is refused.
Created-job cap of 1.
Pending-job cap of 1.
Job identity is unique within a transaction.
An operation outside the registry faults.
Facts hold integers: setting one to a boolean is an invalid value.
A guard comparing true does not match stored integer 1.
A boolean advance target is invalid time.
A string advance target is invalid time.
An advance target before the clock is invalid time.
Arithmetic on a non-integer fact is an invalid operation.
Two rules moving the same item to different places conflict; custody is never duplicated.
Two identical emissions are two deliveries, not deduplicated.

lantern.description: Taking the lantern before the quest exists: activation credits current possession, not a replayed event.
Dropping the lantern after the choice opens rejects the choice; closing it leaves the quest active.
After the schedule moves Bram away, a new choice is rejected and can be closed.
A choice made before Bram moves still replays its receipt afterwards, without restoring the old view.
Changing the ending under a used id conflicts; the original replays and narration is not repeated.
A fault before COMMIT discards every choice consequence; the choice can then resolve.
Unknown COMMIT of the choice, later known absent: retry runs new, one narration.
Unknown COMMIT of the choice, later known committed: retry replays, one narration.
Committed before narration reached memory: recovery restores it once and the retry replays.
Looking changes no time, RNG or game state.
A new choice against an old view and an unavailable exit both leave state unchanged.
